subsystems.name: Signal capture
subsystems.role: collects behaviour from whatever the user is touching, without extra hardware.

subsystems.name: Feature extraction
subsystems.role: turns raw events into compact, comparable numbers.
parts: typing rhythm over a word or phrase

subsystems.name: Behaviour model
subsystems.role: holds a per-user template and scores how well current behaviour matches it.

subsystems.name: Risk fusion engine
subsystems.role: combines the behaviour score with other live signals into one continuous trust value.

subsystems.name: Policy engine
subsystems.role: decides what the trust value means right now.

buildSteps.title: Choose what to sense
buildSteps.detail: Decide which signals are reliable on the target devices — keyboard and pointer on desktops, touch and motion on phones — and where collection happens.

buildSteps.title: Instrument the client
buildSteps.detail: An SDK or browser component emits timestamped events to the feature pipeline, keeping raw keystrokes on the device where possible.

buildSteps.title: Enrol each user
buildSteps.detail: Behaviour is sampled over an initial period so a personal template can be built; enrolment must tolerate people who type unusually little.

buildSteps.title: Engineer features
buildSteps.detail: Intervals, speeds and rhythms are normalised so that a slow day or a new keyboard does not look like an impostor.

buildSteps.title: Train the scorer
buildSteps.detail: A per-user anomaly model is trained alongside population models that recognise generic human versus machine input.

buildSteps.title: Fuse and threshold
buildSteps.detail: The score is combined with device, network and explicit-auth signals, and risk bands are set for allow, challenge and block.

buildSteps.title: Tune false accepts and false rejects
buildSteps.detail: Thresholds are adjusted on real traffic so genuine users are rarely interrupted while impostors are caught.

buildSteps.title: Deploy, monitor and keep learning
buildSteps.detail: The template adapts gradually to genuine drift, while monitoring looks for poisoning, replay or injection of synthetic input.

buildSteps.title: Wire into access control
buildSteps.detail: The policy engine drives step-up prompts, silent re-authentication and session termination through the existing identity system.

prerequisites.why: keyboards, touchscreens and accelerometers already produce the signals, so no new hardware is needed.

prerequisites.tech: Low-latency machine learning at the edge
prerequisites.why: scoring must finish in milliseconds inside the login or session flow.

prerequisites.tech: A strong explicit authenticator to anchor trust
prerequisites.why: behaviour alone drifts; standards such as FIDO2/WebAuthn passkeys give a cryptographic starting point that behaviour then extends.
injected or replayed input can imitate a user, and detection methods are still maturing; presentation-attack standards such as ISO/IEC 30107 cover biometrics more broadly than behaviour.
behavioural data is personal data under privacy law, and there is no settled cross-vendor benchmark for accuracy or fairness.

pathway.milestone: continuous risk scoring running behind online banking and fraud detection
pathway.unlocks: silent, friction-free scrutiny of sessions that today rely on passwords and one-time codes.

pathway.milestone: continuous authentication adopted in enterprise and consumer sign-in alongside passkeys
pathway.unlocks: sessions that re-verify themselves instead of expiring on a timer.

pathway.milestone: common evaluation benchmarks and interoperability between vendors
pathway.unlocks: honest comparison of false-accept rates and fair treatment across typing styles, devices and disabilities.

pathway.milestone: on-device templates bound to hardware attestation
pathway.unlocks: behaviour that never leaves the phone, and trust that can be proven rather than inferred from a central store.
